analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced macro validation HR@10 to 0.4913, versus 0.4987 for the preceding convolutional model and 0.505 for SASRec. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.520, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.560, Electronics 0.345, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.540. Electronics declined from the reported convolutional result of 0.360 and SASRec result of 0.420. These observations do not support adding attention in this configuration; they do not establish why performance declined. Execution consumed 343.69 allocated GPU-seconds. No test results were used.
code_summary: One jointly trained ConvRec per category: 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned item bias, four residual causal convolution blocks with dilations 1/2/4/8, followed by one pre-normalized two-head causal self-attention layer with 0.25 attention dropout and final LayerNorm. Attention masks future and padding keys, safely handles fully masked rows, and zeros padded representations. Training retains random-prefix sampling, 256-negative sampled softmax, a 2,048-token loss cap, AdamW, and validation-based single-checkpoint selection. The generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture, strictly loads exactly one checkpoint per category, and preserves dataset routing. Checks cover finite empty/padded-history outputs, causality, and checkpoint-reload score agreement.
